arxiv-2203-16333.title: On some nested floor functions and their jump discontinuities
arxiv-2203-16333.creator: Luca Onnis
arxiv-2203-16333.description: Abstract . This paper investigates some particular limits involving nested floor functions. We’ll prove some cases and then we’ll show a more general result. Then we’ll count the discontinuity points of those functions, and we’ll prove a method to find them all.

arxiv-2403-11169.title: Correcting misinformation on social media with a large language model
arxiv-2403-11169.creator: Xinyi Zhou, Ashish Sharma, Amy X. Zhang, Tim Althoff
arxiv-2403-11169.description: Abstract Abstract Real-world misinformation, often multimodal, can be partially correct and factual but misleading by cherry-picking, conflating correlation with causation, and using other tactics. Such misinformation is severely understudied, challenging to address, and harms many social domains, including democracy, economics, justice, human rights, and public health, particularly on social media, where it can spread rapidly.

arxiv-2504-18238.title: SecCityVR: Visualization and Collaborative Exploration of Software Vulnerabilities in Virtual Reality Conference: The 29th International Conference on Evaluation and Assessment in Software Engineering; 17–20 June, 2025; Istanbul, Türkiye CCS: Human-centered computing Visualization systems and tools
arxiv-2504-18238.creator: Dennis Wüppelmann, Enes Yigitbas
arxiv-2504-18238.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Dennis Wüppelmann, Enes Yigitbas. Security vulnerabilities in software systems represent significant risks as potential entry points for malicious attacks. Traditional dashboards that display the results of static analysis security testing often use 2D or 3D visualizations, which tend to lack the spatial details required to effectively reveal issues such as the propagation of vulnerabilities across the codebase or the appearance of concurrent vulnerabilities.

arxiv-2505-12783.title: Unimodular equations which do not preserve the derived length of a group
arxiv-2505-12783.creator: Mikhail A. Mikheenko
arxiv-2505-12783.description: Abstract It is a known fact that any unimodular equation over an abelian group has a solution in that group itself. It is also known that for metabelian groups this does not hold; moreover, there is a unimodular equation over some metabelian group which has no solutions in any larger metabelian group.

arxiv-2510-21141.title: TurboTest : Learning When Less is Enough through Early Termination of Internet Speed Tests
arxiv-2510-21141.creator: Haarika Manda, Manshi Sagar, Yogesh, Kartikay Singh, Cindy Zhao, Tarun Mangla, Phillipa Gill, Elizabeth Belding, Arpit Gupta
arxiv-2510-21141.description: Abstract Internet speed tests are indispensable for users, ISPs, and policymakers, but their static flooding-based design imposes growing costs: a single high-speed test can transfer hundreds of MB, and collectively, platforms like Ookla, M-Lab, and Fast.com generate petabytes of traffic each month. Reducing this burden requires deciding when a test can be stopped early without sacrificing accuracy.

arxiv-2512-01879.title: Lyapunov 1-forms on orbifolds
arxiv-2512-01879.creator: Fabricio Valencia
arxiv-2512-01879.description: Abstract . We introduce and analyze a notion of smooth Lyapunov 1-form for flows generated by vector fields on orbifolds. Using asymptotic cycles and chain-recurrent sets, we establish topological conditions that guarantee the existence of a Lyapunov 1-form, lying in a prescribed cohomology class, for a given vector field on a compact orbifold.

arxiv-2602-03222.title: Scalar and Spinor Quasi Normal Modes of a 2D Dilatonic Blackhole
arxiv-2602-03222.creator: Pabitra Gayen, Ratna Koley
arxiv-2602-03222.description: Abstract External non-minimally coupled scalar and spinor field perturbations have been studied in a (1 + 1) dimensional dilatonic blackhole spacetime 23 ; 32 . Exact analytical expressions of the quasi-normal mode frequencies have been found for both the cases. In the scalar perturbations the quasi-normal mode frequencies turn out to be purely imaginary and negative.

arxiv-2602-10972.description: Abstract . In large-scale agile systems development, the lack of a unified requirements engineering (RE) process is a major challenge, exacerbated by the absence of high-level guiding principles for effective requirements management. To address this challenge, we conducted a five-year longitudinal case study with Grundfos AB , in collaboration with the Software Centre in Sweden.

pmc-10499917.title: Combined analysis of 16S rDNA sequencing and metabolomics to find biomarkers of drug-induced liver injury
pmc-10499917.creator: Kaini He, Mimi Liu, Qian Wang, Sijie Chen, Xiaoyan Guo
pmc-10499917.description: Drug induced liver injury (DILI) is a kind of liver dysfunction which caused by drugs, and gut microbiota could affect liver injury. However, the relationship between gut microbiota and its metabolites in DILI patients is not clear. The total gut microbiota DNA was extracted from 28 DILI patient and 28 healthy control volunteers (HC) and 16S rDNA gene were amplified.

The success opened a promising new route toward developing AI models to grasp underlying biological knowledge from massive data to a scale that cannot be handled by human analysis.

pmc-11630726.title: The Substantial Role of Cell and Nanoparticle Surface Properties in the Antibacterial Potential of Spherical Silver Nanoparticles

PurposeAlthough it is well known that the size, shape, and surface chemistry affect the biological potential of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs), the published studies that have considered the influence of AgNP surface on antibacterial activity have not provided conclusive results.

pmc-11666769.title: Radiation dose to the eye of physicians during radio frequency catheter ablation: a small-scale study
pmc-11666769.creator: Yoshiaki Morishima, Koichi Chida, Hiroo Chiba, Koji Kumagai
pmc-11666769.description: BackgroundRadio frequency catheter ablation (RFCA), a treatment for arrhythmia, requires a long fluoroscopy time that increases the radiation exposure dose to the physician, particularly to the lens of the eye. It is recommended that a lens-specific dosimeter such as DOSIRIS® is used to measure the dose to the lens.

pmc-12454101.title: Diffusion models for robotic manipulation: a survey
pmc-12454101.creator: Rosa Wolf, Yitian Shi, Sheng Liu, Rania Rayyes
pmc-12454101.description: Diffusion generative models have demonstrated remarkable success in visual domains such as image and video generation. They have also recently emerged as a promising approach in robotics, especially in robot manipulations. Diffusion models leverage a probabilistic framework, and they stand out with their ability to model multi-modal distributions and their robustness to high-dimensional input and output spaces.

pmc-12556801.title: Biochemical reconstitution of temozolomide-induced mutational processes
pmc-12556801.creator: Mahima R. Sanyal, Tomohiko Sugiyama
pmc-12556801.description: Temozolomide (TMZ), a DNA alkylator, is a chemotherapeutic agent for brain tumors, but the treatment induces a distinct pattern of mutations, known as a cancer mutational signature single-base substitution signature 11 (SBS11). Although the correlation between TMZ treatment and SBS11 mutations is very clear, the precise biochemical mechanisms that cause SBS11 have not been elucidated.

pmc-12558797.title: The role of immune- and lipid metabolism-related genes in macrophage polarization and prognosis of glioblastoma
pmc-12558797.creator: Yue Zhang, Xin Xu, Shuo Li, Chenlong Liao, Xiaosheng Yang, Wenchuan Zhang
pmc-12558797.description: ObjectiveTo investigate the roles of immune- and lipid metabolism-related genes in macrophage polarization and their prognostic and therapeutic implications in glioblastoma (GBM).MethodsA total of 655 GBM samples from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were stratified into immune and non-immune groups based on immune scores.

pmc-12610590.title: Antimicrobial Effects of Chitosan, Mastic Essential Oil and Citric Acid, and Their Combinations on the Spoilage Microbiota of “Guacamole”: An Avocado-Based Salad
pmc-12610590.creator: Rameez Al-Daour, Ayman Zehra Shakir Hussein, Tareq M Osaili, Fayeza Hasan, Dinesh Kumar Dhanasekaran, Mutamed Ayyash, Leila Cheikh Ismail, Thaís Benincá, Patrícia da Silva Malheiros, Ioannis N Savvaidis, Qin Wang, Ivana Generalić Mekinić
pmc-12610590.description: Guacamole is an avocado-based Ready-to-Eat (RTE) salad product, consumed globally and increasingly popular due to health trends. Its composition, characterized by a relatively neutral pH and stable water activity, creates favorable conditions for microbial proliferation, leading to spoilage, and resulting in a limited shelf-life of the product. Natural antimicrobials, such as essential oils (EOs), organic acids, chitosan, etc.

pmc-13235503.title: Structural variation drives praziquantel response and host adaptation in Schistosoma japonicum
pmc-13235503.creator: Qi Liu, Ke Yang, Wei Zhang, Shuhua Xu, Wei Hu, Yan Lu
pmc-13235503.description: SummaryStructural variation (SV) is a major yet underappreciated source of genomic diversity that drives parasite adaptation. We generated the first comprehensive SV map of Schistosoma japonicum from 72 genomes across six endemic Asian regions, identifying 12,632 high-confidence SVs spanning 3.55% of the genome that delineate population structure and adaptive trajectories.

pmc-13273651.title: Mechanobiology of hypertrophic chondrocyte mineralization: Biomechanical regulation and therapeutic implications in skeletal disorders
pmc-13273651.creator: Yuhao Liu, Guangyu Xu, Yi Shen, Shaotian Fu, An Qin
pmc-13273651.description: Chondrocyte proliferation, differentiation and hypertrophic mineralization are central events that guide subsequent vascular invasion and bone replacement processes. This process is controlled by a sophisticated molecular network including transcription factors such as SOX9 and Runx2, as well as key signaling pathways such as Bone Morphogenetic Protein (BMP), Indian Hedgehog (Ihh) and Fibroblast Growth Factor (FGF).

pmc-13346014.title: Normoglycemic High Anion Gap Metabolic Acidosis With Hyperkalemia: An Unusual Presentation of Alcoholic Ketoacidosis
pmc-13346014.creator: Armaan Mishra, Mohammad Shagil, Lakhan Singh
pmc-13346014.description: Alcoholic ketoacidosis (AKA) is a form of high anion gap metabolic acidosis characterized by ketosis, typically occurring in malnourished individuals after binge alcohol consumption. If not identified early, it can lead to life-threatening electrolyte disturbances and cardiac arrhythmias.A man in his fifties presented with altered mental status and shortness of breath.

pmc-13389288.title: Inferred vegans in studies not designed to assess vegan status may be largely artifacts
pmc-13389288.creator: Christian Koeder, Maximilian Andreas Storz
pmc-13389288.description: Recent studies from China and India, none designed to assess vegan status, reported unusually large vegan samples (n = ~1000–8000) and prevalences (~1–9%). These were mostly inferred from short food frequency modules or short-term dietary assessment (e.g., 1 month). Many inferred vegans were socioeconomically marginalized or socially excluded.

pmc-13392990.title: The different routes of parallel evolution in epiarenic growth in a hyperarid desert environment
pmc-13392990.creator: Marcus A. Koch, Christiane Kiefer, Elena Bergmann, Ron Eric Stein, Michael H. J. Barfuss
pmc-13392990.description: The Atacama Desert, one of the driest and oldest regions on Earth, represents an extreme environment that has driven remarkable adaptive evolution over millions of years. Within this setting, the genus Tillandsia comprises specialists capable of surviving at the dry limit of plant life.

pmc-13474267.title: Parent and child-reported acceptability and preference of pediatric home sleep apnea testing versus In-lab polysomnography: a pilot study
pmc-13474267.creator: Anna Scott, Christopher M Cielo, Melissa Xanthopoulos, Ignacio Tapia, Darko Stefanovski, Mahalakshmi Somayaji
pmc-13474267.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesIn-lab polysomnography (PSG) remains the gold standard for the diagnosis of pediatric obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but its limited availability has prompted the exploration of home sleep apnea testing (HSAT) with encephalogram (EEG) in children. While the feasibility and accuracy of HSAT have been studied previously in children, parent- and child-reported acceptability and preferences of HSAT compared with PSG are unknown.

pmc-13608305.title: Multi-Pathway Antifungal Mechanism of Marine-Derived Bacillus sp. BAF143 Against Aspergillus flavus
pmc-13608305.creator: Xiaoyun Ou, Youzhi Li, Shaojie Wang, Qiaozhen Wang, Shushi Huang, Futian Yu, Yuening Luo, Min Liang, Ling Yang, Lixia Pan, Xiaochun Wang, Dengfeng Yang
pmc-13608305.description: Aspergillus flavus is a major fungal pathogen that causes postharvest spoilage and carcinogenic aflatoxin contamination in agricultural commodities, necessitating the development of novel biocontrol strategies. In this study, a bacterial strain of Bacillus sp. BAF143, isolated from a Martin medium plate used for marine fungal cultivation, exhibited potent antifungal activity against A. flavus.

uslaw-usc-t18-s2074.title: 18 U.S.C. § 2074 — False weather reports
uslaw-usc-t18-s2074.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s2074.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part I (Crimes); Chapter 101 (Records And Reports). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Whoever knowingly issues or publishes any counterfeit weather forecast or warning of weather conditions falsely representing such forecast or warning to have been issued or published by the Weather Bureau, United States Signal Service, or other branch of the Government.
